text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - President Michal Kovac refused to sign the controversial law on the protection of republic, saying the proposed legislation was in contradiction to constitution, and returned it to parliament for revision.

- The Czech bank Agrobanka is expected to sell its Slovak branch to a consortium of four Slovak chemical companies and one commercial bank. The new bank is expected to launch activities with the basic capital of one billion crowns in the first quarter of this year.
- Overall tax burden for enterpreneurs in Slovakia is gradualy increasing, totalling 45 percent last year, compared with 44.4 percent in 1995 and 36.8 percent in 1993.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The state-run Slovak Railways s.p. are expected to be transformed to a 100-percent state-owned joint-stock company at the beginning of 1998.
- A free-trade agreement between Slovakia and Israel, removing custom protection on almost all trade articles, comes to effect from the beginning of this year.

- J.P. Morgan ranks first among financial institutions which have managed syndicated loans for Slovak subjects, accounting for 31 percent of the market. ING Barings ranks second with a roughly 21 percent share.

- The major Slovak car dealer Drukos s.r.o. will on January 15 issue a 250 million crown tranche of five year bonds, lead managed by Slovenska Sporitelna. The bond will carry a fixed annual coupon of 13.5 percent.
SME - President Kovac said he supported an idea of direct citizen vote of the president, compared with the current system where the head of the state is elected by the parliament.
- Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar believes that there would not be an early election this year.
